entities.tagline: An agentic automation that monitors a PR, resolves merge conflicts, keeps CI green, and addresses review feedback until the PR is ready, while pushing back on unreasonable requests.
entities.longDescription: Boyle demonstrates agent merge, one of the options Copilot offers (alongside create PR and create draft PR) when opening a pull request. The agent periodically polls the PR, fixes merge conflicts, monitors CI and pushes changes until it's green, and responds to feedback from both agents like Copilot code review and human reviewers. Once everything is green and approval is granted, it merges the PR. He frames it for low-risk, functional changes where minor review feedback can be trusted to the agent, showing the first-ever agent merge PR from Jeremy, its creator, which adds a health check verifying the GH CLI is installed at app startup.

firstMention.sessionTitle: Why your AI code doesn’t ship: Closing the gap to production

entities.tagline: A managed, PostgreSQL-compatible open-source database supporting large-scale OLTP, alongside Cosmos DB on the backend
entities.longDescription: Azure HorizonDB is a new PostgreSQL database whose public preview was announced the prior day by Satya [inferred Nadella]. It takes the open-source PostgreSQL engine and connects it to a cloud-optimized scalable storage backend to achieve higher resiliency, larger scale, and better performance for Postgres workloads. It is designed for the new era of AI agents, shipping with built-in AI models, AI pipelines, and AI functions.

firstMention.sessionTitle: Simplify app dev with cloud-native PostgreSQL in Azure HorizonDB

entities.tagline: Agent-drivable, bidirectional UI surfaces (terminal, browser, triage boards, whiteboards, Kanban) that users or the agent can author dynamically and check into the repo's `.github` folder for team sharing.
entities.longDescription: Canvases are agent-drivable UI surfaces within the Copilot app that the agent can fully drive on the right-hand side of the app, including a terminal canvas and a web browser. The agent can open the terminal, send commands, read output, open the browser, and perform automated testing in response to natural-language prompts. The demo showed asking the agent to open the terminal canvas, run a web server rendering 'Hello canvas', and then open the browser to render that page. Canvases support a rich bidirectional relationship and enable users to build their own customized views and workflows.

entities.tagline: A multi-mode agent (advisor and critic) available in the Copilot CLI and Copilot app for getting a second opinion on work.
entities.longDescription: Boyle introduces rubber duck, presented alongside slash review (code review) and slash security review, as a way to combine multiple models duking it out with each other. He kicks off a workflow using the Create Session tool to spawn two sessions—one for security review and one for code review—running Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.5, and Gemini in parallel sub agents, then uses Rubber Duck to critique the feedback and turn it into PR comments. Security review is powered by tech from GitHub Advanced Security and code review by Copilot code review. He also demonstrates a private "rubber duck" agent thread in PR review mode for quickly building context on a change.

entities.tagline: A developer-first GPU machine with the NVIDIA RTX Spark [inferred] offering up to 1 petaflop of AI compute and 128GB of unified memory, preconfigured with the developer tools by default
entities.longDescription: Microsoft announced the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box, a developer "dream machine" that maxes out compute and memory on the new architecture. It delivers one petaflop of AI compute, 20 CPU cores, and 128 GB of unified memory access. It is coming in the fall, and attendees can join a waitlist. This follows the earlier Surface Ultra device that pairs NVIDIA power with Surface design, featuring 128 GB unified memory, a 2,000-nit display, and all-day battery life.
